events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Southeast winds 35 to 45 mph with gusts up to 55 mph
expected.

* WHERE...Unalaska and Nikolski.

* WHEN...From 7 PM this evening to 10 PM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects and a few
power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A strong low pressure system in the southern
Bering will bring strong westerly winds beginning this evening and
continuing through Friday evening. The strongest wind gusts up to
55 mph are likely through westerly favored gaps near Unalaska.
Winds to steadily diminish through late Friday night.

events.summary:
* WHAT...Southeast winds 25 to 40 mph with gusts 45 to 60 mph.
Localized gusts up to 75 mph for Akutan and 85 mph for Cold Bay.

* WHERE...Aleutians East Borough.

* WHEN...Until 11 AM AKDT this morning.

* IMPACTS...High winds may move loose debris, damage property, and
cause power outages. Travel will be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A strong front and low pressure system will
move across the Alaska Peninsula this morning. Expect strong
southerly wind gusts with the highest gusts around Cold Bay and
westerly gusts around Akutan. Winds will quickly turn westerly
later this morning and will slowly diminish before turning
southerly and becoming gusty again, with gusts 40 to 60 mph, this
evening.

events.summary:
* WHAT...West winds 45 to 65 mph with gusts up to 80 mph expected.

* WHERE...Atka and Adak.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM AKDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...High winds may move loose debris, damage property, and
cause power outages. Travel will be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Very strong westerly winds will initiate this
morning due to a deep low pressure system in the southern Bering
Sea. Favored East-West channels could promote locally higher gusts.
Strongest winds are expected from about noon to 3pm AKDT. Winds to
steadily diminish through tonight.

events.summary:
* WHAT...Southeast winds 40 to 50 mph with gusts up to 70 mph
expected. Localized wind gusts up to 75 mph near Cape Newenham.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island and Western Capes.

* WHEN...Until 1 AM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects and a few
power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A strong front moving inland from the eastern
Bering will bring gusty southeasterly winds to the Kuskokwim Delta
coast and the Western Capes through this morning. Winds are
expected to peak around noon today, then steadily diminish through
this evening. Following this system, another round of gusty
southerly winds are expected Friday morning, with wind gusts as
high as 50 mph.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Arecibo in Puerto Rico...
Ciales in Puerto Rico...
Florida in Puerto Rico...
Jayuya in Puerto Rico...
Utuado in Puerto Rico...

* WHEN...Until 400 PM AST.

* IMPACTS...Rises in small streams and normally dry arroyos.
Dangerous flows over low-water crossings. Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 101 PM AST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This  will cause urban and small stream flooding.
Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...One to two feet of inundation above ground level in low-
lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Ocean, Atlantic, Cape May and Southeastern Burlington.

* WHEN...Until 2 AM EDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...At this level, widespread roadway flooding occurs in
coastal and bayside communities and along inland tidal
waterways. Many roads become impassable. Some damage to
vulnerable structures may begin to occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Moderate tidal flooding could continue
into the weekend. Cannot rule out major tidal flooding
impacts, especially within Barnegat Bay.

grouped_sources.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, one to two feet of
inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory,
large breaking waves of up to 12 feet in the surf zone. For
the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Delaware Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 2 AM EDT Saturday.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 8 PM EDT Saturday. For the
High Rip Current Risk, through Saturday evening.

* IMPACTS...At this level, widespread roadway flooding occurs in
coastal and bayside communities and along inland tidal
waterways. Many roads become impassable. Some damage to
vulnerable structures may begin to occur. Dangerous swimming
and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Significant beach erosion is expected.
Breaching of sand dunes is possible. Moderate tidal flooding
could continue into the weekend. Cannot rule out major tidal
flooding impacts, especially around Rehoboth Bay and Indian
River.

large breaking waves of up to 11 feet in the surf zone. For
the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

For the High Rip Current Risk, through Saturday evening.

* IMPACTS...At this level, flooding begins on the most

localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS... Localized moderate tidal flooding
impacts cannot be ruled out. Widespread minor tidal flooding
could continue into the weekend.
